correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies in the southwestern headward/highland sector. The historical NTS mosaic depicts marsh/swamp ground, contours, scattered small water bodies and sparse stream/gully linework here. It does not demonstrate an unambiguous continuous channel itinerary from the actual selected opening into the recognizable Kaskattama valley. The primary2017 report places Kaskattama headwaters on the Kaskattama highland, but this general statement and its regional hillshade map do not prove this particular feeder. No source lake or opening-stream hydronym is established.

The original topographic linework depicts a recognizable northeastward river valley with branching/narrow watercourse reaches on the northwest side of the highland, continuing toward the broader eastward upper-middle bend. Bouchard Lake and Burgess Lake are separately depicted in the adjacent highland, south/east of that receiving corridor; no selected through-lake itinerary through either is established. The source-supported valley continuation does not itself establish how the selected far-southwestern beginning reaches it.
correspondence.selected_component_role: mapped upper receiving trunk after the unresolved initial interval

correspondence.component_scope: eastward upper middle bend and join
correspondence.finding: The mapped trunk follows the broad eastward turn and then bends northeast/north into the repeated Kaskattama-labelled corridor. Kitin Creek is separately labelled on a western tributary entering this upper-middle river network. The selected trunk is a fluvial corridor beside scattered lakes and wetland symbols, rather than a chain through the nearby named highland lakes.

Repeated Kaskattama River lettering follows the northward and northeastward meandering trunk through extensive marsh/swamp lowlands. The characteristic northward reach, westward kink and ensuing northeastward valley are depicted. Small tributaries enter from both sides; the western lake-and-creek field includes a separately labelled Minaker Creek corridor. Those side-component names are not assigned to the selected trunk.

correspondence.component_scope: lower meanders and major western joins
correspondence.finding: The mapped lower river continues northeast through broad loops, narrow side channels and wetland ground. Several substantial western tributary channels can be followed into it; the map also depicts many detached or adjacent small lakes. No major lake, reservoir or dam interrupts the observed selected lower trunk. Individual tributary/side-channel labels are not normalized into a uniform Kaskattama name.

The directly labelled Kaskattama lower river crosses the joined map-sheet latitude edge and reaches Hudson Bay east of Cape Tatnam. The mouth is depicted as a branched/widened coastal outlet, with coastal marsh and beach-ridge terrain around it. This establishes the actual receiving-water setting and distinguishes the route from the Black Duck and Kettle corridors farther east. No exact modern bank, tidal limit or terminal vertex is asserted.

The observed upper receiving valley and middle/lower trunk run through marsh/swamp terrain with small side waters and larger off-route highland lakes. No major selected through-lake passage or reservoir is established in that mapped interval. The initial feeder/wetland connector remains unresolved, so the review cannot make a whole-selected-route statement about all headward water links.

correspondence.component_scope: western headward stream and first lake/steady entry
correspondence.finding: Figure50 shows the north-to-south initial small stream west of the longer northern lake-fed branch, entering the western side of the broad southwestern lake/steady complex. Its position relative to that complex, the eastern outlet and the northern arm corresponds to the selected opening and initial southward bend. The unnamed feeder is not renamed Kenamu.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component scale; no exact headpoint or bank assertion

correspondence.component_scope: upper western lake/steady passage and northern-arm junction
correspondence.finding: The western broad waterbody narrows eastward into the outgoing trunk. A distinct substantial branch descends from the north through its own broadened/lake-fed reaches and joins before the trunk bends southeast. The selected route uses the western lake/steady arm and the outgoing trunk, rather than adopting the separate northern branch as its headwater. Smaller side ponds and linked tributaries remain separate features.
correspondence.correspondence: complete; connected waterbody/stream links are visually depicted, with their individual hydronyms unestablished

correspondence.component_scope: southeast upper trunk and Little Drunken River junction
correspondence.finding: Figure50 follows the selected southeastward outlet corridor to its southern bend, where the distinct tributary T56 joins from the south. The figure key identifies T56 as Little Drunken River, and printed page158 independently states that the Kenamu turns north at this confluence. The selected route remains on the outgoing Kenamu corridor rather than taking T56.

correspondence.component_scope: northward middle valley and major tributaries
correspondence.finding: The mapped trunk continues north/northeast past separate western lake-fed tributaries and the eastern T40 junction. The figure key identifies T40 as Salmon River. A further downstream eastern tributary is labelled T31 without a hydronym. The first numbered mainstem rapid lies between T40 and T31, consistently with the prose and obstruction table. These junctions and the long northward valley match the selected middle corridor.
correspondence.correspondence: complete; no current fish passage or flow conditions inferred

correspondence.component_scope: lower river and actual receiving water
correspondence.finding: The original map continues the river beyond T31 through its long lower northward reach and final bends, widening at the Lake Melville shore. Printed page158 and Table206 identify Lake Melville as the receiving water. The stored terminal class sea is interpreted geographically as this Lake Melville inlet setting; the selected line is not asserted to end directly on the open Labrador Sea.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at river-to-receiving-water scale; exact present shoreline, channel banks and estuarine boundary unestablished

correspondence.finding: Southern opening lies in/beside the Alto Turiaçu Indigenous-land and Centro Novo/Nova Olinda/Maranhãozinho setting before extending north through the Centro do Guilherme corridor. The northern portion is depicted and repeatedly labelled Rio Maracaçumé on the Maracaçumé2010 original. It follows the northbound course past tributary joins, the Maracaçumé urban/road crossing setting and the northeastward municipal-edge corridor into the next fragment. The selected route is distinguished from the separate Maracaçumezinho transverse course. The whole initial southern channel and its northward connector to that mapped Maracaçumé portion are not established on readable original cartography. Nearby labels, the broad river basin and the model chain do not resolve this interval.
correspondence.headward_setting: Southern opening lies in/beside the Alto Turiaçu Indigenous-land and Centro Novo/Nova Olinda/Maranhãozinho setting before extending north through the Centro do Guilherme corridor.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: No mapped lake or reservoir passage was observed in the established northern interval. Waterbody/branch continuity in the unread initial interval remains unresolved.
correspondence.material_gap: The whole initial southern channel and its northward connector to that mapped Maracaçumé portion are not established on readable original cartography. Nearby labels, the broad river basin and the model chain do not resolve this interval.

correspondence.finding: The channel continues north and northeast along the Maracaçumé/Cândido Mendes and Amapá do Maranhão eastern-edge setting, with incoming side drainage and progressive widening toward the lower river. The adjoining Maracaçumé, Amapá do Maranhão and southern/northern Cândido Mendes map coverage was read across the fragment. Rio Tromaí is a distinct western drainage, not the selected mainstem.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: No lake or reservoir connector is needed to account for this mapped river interval. The lower end approaches the coastal wetland/tidal-river setting.

correspondence.finding: The lower channel runs through the Cândido Mendes/Vila Gracinha and Feitoria setting, divides and rejoins around a small mangrove island, and proceeds north through the Jardim/Ponta do Jardim tidal corridor. Lateral channels communicate with the widening estuary; their own names are not inferred from the main candidate.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Coastal mangrove/alluvial and salt-marsh setting with tidal splits/joins; not a lake or reservoir chain.
correspondence.actual_terminal: The retained endpoint lies in widened estuarine water, beside a lateral eastward estuarine arm leading toward the Igarapé Pinto setting. Wider original cartography depicts communication with Oceano Atlântico. The retained model sea terminal is not interpreted as an exact surveyed shoreline mouth.

correspondence.finding: The 04/2021 original depicts the selected opening south of the protected-land boundary as a small unlabelled drainage turning east and then southeast. It continues through successive side-stream joins west of the separately labelled Camapi do Maracá/Repartimento/Pimentel tributary group. The feeder reaches the southern bend and a west-arriving river at the Varador do Maracá setting. The 2007 northern and southern panels show the corresponding drainage continuation across their adjoining margins.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary feeder/corridor scale; headward name null.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: No selected lake or reservoir traversal is depicted in this upper feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: Varador joining bend and northeast middle course
correspondence.finding: The 04/2021 original labels the west-arriving river Rio Maracá-Pucu beside the Varador setting. From this joining area the mapped course bends northeast and continues to the northern tributary convergence and Pacu do Maracá setting. Both originals depict the northern Camapi do Maracá tributary system and distinguish its Repartimento/Pimentel branches from the selected western approach.
correspondence.correspondence: Joining bend, northeast return and material northern convergence established; no tributary-name transfer to the selected opening.

correspondence.finding: After the northeast reach the mapped trunk turns south and east through the Pancada/Pedra Chata and Pançudo/Maracá settlement corridor. The originals show continuous drainage through the lowland middle course and western tributary joins toward Boa Esperança. The 04/2021 compilation adds the Central do Maracá, São Miguel, Lagoa do Maracá and Barro Alto locality setting. The model line is generalized westward through part of this sector; the evidence is corridor correspondence rather than an exact plotted channel-by-channel match.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete ordinary corridor interpretation; precise parallel lowland channel choice remains outside the naming claim.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Locality labels containing Lago/Lagoa are not converted into lake-name or lake-traversal claims.

correspondence.component_scope: Adjacent lake complex and lower continuation
correspondence.finding: The 04/2021 original shows a broad lobed waterbody complex east of Boa Esperança and beside Poção do Rio Preto/Tabatinga. The selected corridor follows the Maracá side to its west and then continues south into the Mangueira–Santa Luzia do Maracá lower setting. The separate Rio Preto proceeds to its own more northerly Amazon-channel mouth. A selected passage across the broad Rio Preto waterbody is not shown or inferred.
correspondence.correspondence: Selected river continuation and separation from the adjacent lake/Rio Preto system established.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Adjacent lobed waterbody and side drainage are read as local context, not as a selected through-lake transfer. No reservoir identified.

correspondence.finding: The lower river widens and splits around small lowland islands/loops before turning northeast. Both originals print Rio Maracá-Pucu on this lower course. The 04/2021 map places the receiving water in Canal do Norte beside Ilha do Pará; the 2007 original shows the floodable Amazon margin and the Maracá-Pucu opening, with the separate Rio Preto mouth farther north and the Ajuruxi/Furo do Maracá setting farther south. The selected terminal is the Maracá-Pucu opening into the north Amazon estuarine channel.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary mouth/distributary-corridor scale; no precise distributary boundary or tide-direction assertion.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Floodable estuarine margin and local split channels; no direct open-ocean coast substituted for the actual receiving channel.
